newsitem.title: USA: CME live, feeder cattle called steady-.15 ct lower.
newsitem.headline: CME live, feeder cattle called steady-.15 ct lower.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures were called steady to 0.15 cent per lb lower with talk of poor holiday weekend meat sales likely to prompt early selling, analysts and traders said.

Cool, damp weather over much of the Midwest particularly, may have played a role in curbing meat buying for cookouts, they said. One analyst relayed talk that weekend meat sales at one store chain were off a third from last year's Memorial Day weekend.
"It was probably not a good weekend for the meat market," said another analyst.
Feedlot interests reported light packer bidding early Tuesday at $65.00 per cwt versus $66.00 sales late last week.
Also, cash beef prices were lower Friday. USDA beef cutout values slipped $0.02 to $0.36 per cwt.
Feeder cattle futures were expected to follow the direction in live cattle, traders said. The latest CME feeder cattle index was down $0.09 at $76.17 per cwt.
